## Office cleaning Newcastle: make the standard visible

A useful office cleaning agreement says what will be cleaned, how often, what is excluded and how issues will be resolved. That is more useful than comparing two prices against an undefined promise of a “standard clean”.

This guide helps a Newcastle office manager, business owner or workplace coordinator prepare the brief, compare proposals and review the result. YOS's commercial cleaning service covers **Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie**. Confirm the actual address and requirements with the team before planning a service.

**Use the working pack:** [Download the Workplace Cleaning Brief & Comparison Checklist (PDF)](/guides/workplace-cleaning-scope-checklist.pdf). It contains 12 checks, a room/task/frequency schedule, a proposal comparison and an issue-review log. Print it or annotate it in your PDF app. No email is required to read it.

For the service itself, visit [office and commercial cleaning with YOS](/cleaning) or [request a site-specific cleaning quote](/cleaning#cleaning-quote-form).

## 1. Walk the office before setting the scope

Start with the actual rooms and how they are used. Record reception, work areas, meeting rooms, kitchens, washrooms, storage, internal glass and any shared spaces. Note approximate area where known, floor types, access restrictions, occupancy and busy periods.

Separate the tenant's areas from common facilities handled by the landlord or building manager. For a Newcastle CBD tenancy, confirm arrangements for shared amenities, waste rooms, lifts and after-hours access. Those responsibilities vary by building; they should not be assumed from the postcode.

A quieter office used a few days a week can need a different schedule from a visitor-facing workplace with heavily used amenities. Floor area is one input, not a complete cleaning brief. Mark requirements that need a site inspection rather than guessing.

## 2. Write tasks, frequency and acceptance together

Avoid a single line saying “clean kitchen” or “clean all offices”. List the task and surface, the visit pattern and the result expected. The schedule below illustrates how to frame the conversation; it is not a prescribed frequency or a default inclusion in every YOS quote.

| Area | Tasks to discuss | Frequency and standard to agree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reception and meeting rooms | Accessible surfaces, agreed touchpoints, floors and internal glass | Match visits and periodic detail to use and presentation needs |
| Workstations | Agreed accessible surfaces, bins and floor areas | Define clear-desk expectations and items that must not be moved |
| Kitchen and break room | Benches, sink, agreed appliance surfaces, bins and floors | Separate routine surfaces from appliance interiors or detail work |
| Washrooms and amenities | Fixtures, surfaces, floors and consumable checks | Define the tasks, stock responsibilities and review arrangement |
| Floors and edges | Vacuuming or hard-floor care, with periodic work separately listed | Confirm material suitability and any specialist treatment scope |
| Internal glass and detail areas | Agreed reachable glass, skirtings and other detail tasks | Specify periodic tasks rather than assuming every visit includes them |

For every line, record **regular visit**, **periodic**, **separately quoted**, or **excluded**. Then agree the actual frequency after the provider has assessed the workplace. An unchecked item is an open question, not an automatic inclusion.

## 3. Separate routine, detail and specialist work

Routine cleaning and a full detail clean are different scopes. Ask what changes between them. If you need carpet steam cleaning, appliance interiors, high-level work, external windows or a post-FitOut handover clean, list those explicitly and confirm suitability, access and availability.

For a handover clean, establish when construction and dusty work will be finished, who authorises access and what readiness checks are needed. A builder's clean does not automatically establish the ongoing office-cleaning scope. See our [FitOut handover checklist](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist) to connect those workstreams.

Medical, food-handling, childcare, hazardous materials and other specialist environments can require different procedures and expertise. Do not assume an ordinary office-cleaning checklist meets those requirements. Identify the need and have the responsible specialists confirm the appropriate scope and provider.

## 4. Compare quotations against the same schedule

Issue the same room and task schedule to each provider. Compare visit frequency, periodic work, exclusions, products, consumables, waste handling, access and quality-review arrangements alongside the price. Ask whether GST is included and how changes or separately requested work are charged.

| Compare | Clarification to request |
| --- | --- |
| Visits and tasks | Which tasks occur at each visit and which have a separate cycle? |
| Products and equipment | Who supplies them, where are they stored and are they suitable for the surfaces? |
| Consumables and waste | Who supplies liners, paper and soap; where does waste go; what is excluded? |
| Access and operating hours | What service window, inductions, keys and building requirements are assumed? |
| Periodic or extra work | Is it included, allowed for, separately priced or unavailable? |
| Service management | Who is the contact, how is cover arranged and how are issues reviewed? |
| Commercial terms | What are the validity, commencement, payment, change and cancellation terms? |

A lower total can represent fewer visits or omitted work. Ask for a revised written proposal after material clarifications so you can compare the actual offers. Keep the agreed scope revision with the final proposal.

## 5. Agree access and security without circulating codes

Nominate a workplace contact and agree service windows, occupied areas, alarm handling, key custody and a process if access fails. Store sensitive codes separately and share them only through the agreed secure process with authorised people. They do not belong in the general quote checklist or an open email chain.

Identify restricted rooms, confidential paperwork, screens, equipment and surfaces that must not be touched. Agree a clear-desk approach where needed and explain how changed access or a one-off event should be communicated.

For after-hours cleaning, ask who confirms the building is secured at the end of the visit and how an incident or urgent issue is reported. The details should suit the actual site and building-management arrangements.

## 6. Ask about safe products and site instructions

Provide information about delicate finishes, equipment restrictions and relevant site hazards. Ask the provider how products are selected for the surfaces, how instructions are followed and how required safety information is made available. SafeWork NSW guidance covers labelling and safety data sheets for hazardous chemicals.

This guide does not prescribe chemical mixes, disinfection methods or infection-control procedures. Those require the right product instructions, site assessment and competent people. A general “eco-friendly” or “safe” label should not replace specific information about the proposed products and use.

## 7. Set a quality-review process that can be used

Agree which parts of the written scope will be checked, who reviews them and how often. Use observable tasks rather than an undefined rating such as “good enough”. A review might record a missed scheduled task, an inaccessible area, a change in use or an item needing separate attention.

Keep an issue log with the date, location, agreed task, issue, contact, action and confirmation of close-out. Photos may help where appropriate, but keep staff information, confidential documents and screens out of them. Agree the response and escalation process with the provider rather than assuming a universal deadline.

Consistency is supported by a documented scope, site notes, communication and handover when people change. Ask how absences or replacement staff are managed; a responsible service conversation should account for them without guaranteeing the same person is always available.

## The 12-point office cleaning checklist

1. Map the areas included and those handled by the landlord or another provider.
2. Record occupancy, visitor patterns, busy periods and service windows.
3. List tasks and surfaces for each area.
4. Agree a site-specific frequency for routine and periodic tasks.
5. Document inclusions, exclusions, products, consumables and waste responsibilities.
6. Confirm timing, occupied areas and building-access requirements.
7. Agree secure arrangements for keys and alarms; keep codes out of the brief.
8. Flag delicate finishes, restricted spaces and requirements outside ordinary office cleaning.
9. Compare providers using the same scope revision.
10. Name workplace and provider contacts and the escalation route.
11. Agree review points, observable standards and issue follow-up.
12. Confirm the final scope, commencement arrangements and first review.

[Use the scope and quality-review pack](/guides/workplace-cleaning-scope-checklist.pdf) to record the details with your provider. For changing use or occupancy, see [reviewing a cleaning scope for a busier office](/blog/commercial-cleaning-scope-busier-office).

## Common Newcastle office cleaning questions

### How often should our office be cleaned?

Frequency depends on use, occupancy, amenities, visitor patterns and presentation needs. Walk the site with the provider and agree frequencies by task and area. A single standard schedule does not suit every workplace.

### How much does office cleaning in Newcastle cost?

A useful price depends on a defined task list, visit pattern, site condition, access and exclusions. Compare proposals against the same schedule and obtain a site-specific quote rather than relying on an unsupported local hourly rate.

### Can cleaning happen after hours?

YOS can agree timing and access during the site inspection. Confirm alarms, keys, occupied areas and building-management requirements before commencement. Availability and arrangements are agreed for the actual site.

### Does YOS cover the whole Hunter region?

The current commercial cleaning service covers Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie. Send the exact address so the team can confirm the site and scope before preparing a proposal.

## Prepare a useful cleaning enquiry

Share the site suburb, workplace type, areas, preferred schedule and the main issue you want resolved. You do not need to guess every task before speaking to the team. Sarah oversees the cleaning service and quality-management pathway; the written proposal confirms the site's scope and arrangements.

[Request an office cleaning quote](/cleaning#cleaning-quote-form) or [meet the YOS team](/about). Start with the scope, then use the checklist to keep expectations visible.

## Go deeper on price and changeover

If you are replacing a provider, the [cleaning changeover plan](/blog/switch-commercial-cleaning-company-newcastle) covers scope, access, starting condition and the first review.
